remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
Now that the base open weights AI models are getting far better, and post training infra is becoming more mature and commercialized, there are going to be all new plays for companies that have large amounts of data to have their own models.

Licensing data for external model training was previously the only play if you had a large corpus of information, but you can now reasonably go and train your own models as well without incurring the cost and complexity of competing with the labs on research.

The general purpose frontier models will still have a leg up in broad areas due to the ability to handle the widest set of tasks, but you can absolutely see a future where we have far more models than today across every vertical and domain.
remarks.translation: 既然基础开放权重AI模型正在变得好得多，而后训练基础设施也日趋成熟和商业化，对于那些拥有大量数据的公司来说，将会出现全新的玩法，让他们能够拥有自己的模型。过去，如果你拥有庞大的信息语料库，授权数据用于外部模型训练是唯一的选择，但现在你完全可以合理地去训练自己的模型，而不必承担与研究实验室竞争的成本和复杂性。通用前沿模型在广泛领域仍将占据优势，因为它们能够处理最广泛的任务集，但你绝对可以预见一个未来：在各个垂直领域和行业中，模型数量将远比今天多得多。

remarks.name: Guillermo Rauch
remarks.role: vercel CEO
remarks.text:
Coding tokens are basically infrastructure. Yet, the way companies have approached them amounts to:

"Hey all, here's an AWS key. It can spin up anything from a 𝚝𝟹.𝚗𝚊𝚗𝚘 (＄𝟹.𝟾𝟶/𝚖𝚘) to an 𝚙𝟻.𝟺𝟾𝚡𝚕𝚊𝚛𝚐𝚎 (＄𝟺𝟶𝚔/𝚖𝚘). Go wild"

And obviously the reason companies don't do this for their core infra is that you need to govern, optimize, and observe usage and costs.

The intern might decide to host a static website in that 192 vCPU machine, and you won't be very happy about the bill.

AI Gateway fixes this for all your tokens, with per-key, and now per-user budgets.
remarks.translation: 编码令牌本质上就是基础设施。然而，公司对待它们的方式却相当于：“嘿，各位，这里有一个AWS密钥。它可以从一个𝚝𝟹.𝚗𝚊𝚗𝚘（＄𝟹.𝟾𝟶/月）扩展到𝚙𝟻.𝟺𝟾𝚡𝚕𝚊𝚛𝚐𝚎（＄𝟺𝟶𝚔/月）。尽情使用吧。”显然，公司不会对自己的核心基础设施这样做，原因在于你需要治理、优化，并监控使用情况和成本。实习生可能会决定在那台192 vCPU的机器上托管一个静态网站，而你看到账单时就不会太高兴了。AI Gateway通过按密钥，以及现在按用户预算的方式，解决了你所有令牌的这个问题。

remarks.name: Dan Shipper
remarks.role: ceo every
remarks.text:
Anthropomorphization of AI is good when it serves to help us use (understand, predict, etc) AI better. 

It’s bad when it serves to sow panic, fear, and unrealistic / unwarranted comparisons to human beings. 

Most opponents of anthropomorphism are rightly reacting to its misuse to sow panic or alter the moral status of agents by claiming consciousness etc. 

It’s possible to use anthropomorphism without doing that though
remarks.translation: 将AI拟人化，当它有助于我们更好地使用（理解、预测等）AI时，这是有益的。而当它被用来散布恐慌、恐惧，以及进行不切实际或无根据的与人类的比较时，则是有害的。大多数反对拟人化的人，正是合理地针对其被滥用以制造恐慌，或通过声称意识等来改变主体的道德地位。然而，我们完全可以在不这样做的前提下，合理运用拟人化。

podcasts.originalTitle: 🔬“We have foundation models for language, not for physics” — Anima Anandkumar, Bren Professor of Computing
podcasts.excerpt: 几年前，加州理工学院教授、Accelerated Understanding联合创始人Anima Anandkumar着手开发首个基于AI的开源天气模型。在与该领域专家交流时，她遇到了质疑。天气是混沌的，物理模拟很难，已经发展了几十年，并且需要超级计算机，数据根本不够。尽管有这些保留意见，Anima还是继续前进并开始构建。不到一年，她的团队就开发出了FourCastNet，一个能与现有最佳物理模拟相媲美的预测模型。多亏了Anima及其后续工作，现在任何人都可以使用消费级GPU在短时间尺度上准确预测天气。在我们发布的约十五集科学节目中，<a target="_blank" href="http://latent.…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs. In the fifteen or so science episodes we’ve released on <a target="_blank" href="http://latent.…
